steps: Dice the bell pepper and mince the garlic. Trim the green beans and halve them. Grate the tomato on a box grater and discard the skin.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pan. Brown the chicken thigh pieces for 4-5 minutes, then remove them.
Add the bell pepper and garlic and cook 2 minutes, then the grated tomato and the paprika, and fry it down to a dark sofrito, about 5 minutes.

Crumble the saffron into 180 ml of warm water or broth and let it steep. Add the short-grain rice, spread it evenly across the pan, pour in the saffron liquid and stir once. Season with salt and black pepper.
Return the chicken and add the green beans and green peas. Do not stir again.

Simmer 18-20 minutes until the rice has absorbed the liquid, adding the shrimp for the last 5 minutes. Raise the heat to high for the final 2 minutes until you hear the base crackle - that is the socarrat. Rest 5 minutes before serving.

note: Added saffron, the defining seasoning, which was absent entirely. Liquid corrected from 2 cups (~8:1) to 180 ml, roughly 3x the rice, so the 'simmer until absorbed' instruction can actually complete. Added the socarrat finish. Chicken Breast -> Chicken Thigh (breast strings out over a 20-minute simmer). Onion removed per Valencian practice and Tomato Sauce -> grated fresh Tomato for the sofrito. Paprika deliberately NOT upgraded to Smoked Paprika - Valencian paella uses sweet pimenton.

steps: Peel and devein the shrimp. Slice the garlic thinly.

Heat the olive oil in a small skillet or earthenware cazuela over low heat. Add the sliced garlic and cook gently 3-4 minutes until pale gold and fragrant - do not let it brown or the oil turns bitter.
Raise the heat, add the shrimp and the chili flakes, and cook 1-2 minutes per side until pink and just curled. Season with salt and black pepper.
Off the heat, pour in the dry sherry and stir in the dried parsley, swirling the pan to emulsify the oil.
Squeeze the lemon over the shrimp and toast the whole wheat bread.
Serve immediately in the pan, still sizzling, with the toasted bread for mopping up the garlic oil.

note: Removed the invented spinach bed - gambas al ajillo is served in its own garlic oil, not plated over greens. Olive oil 15 -> 25 g: the oil IS the sauce here and 1 tbsp for 200 g of shrimp misses the dish, but 25 g is a deliberate compromise short of the traditional 30-45 g given the app's macro budget. Garlic now coaxed over LOW heat (the burnt-garlic failure mode) and shrimp timing halved to 1-2 min/side. Added parsley (the canonical finish) and a splash of dry sherry. Lemon kept - sources describe it as a live disagreement among Spanish cooks, not an error.

steps: Peel the potato and slice it thinly, about 2-3 mm. Slice the onion finely.

Heat the olive oil in a non-stick skillet over low heat and add the potato and onion. Cook gently 15-20 minutes, turning occasionally, until completely tender - they should poach in the oil, not brown or crisp. Drain, reserving the oil.
Beat the eggs with salt and black pepper in a large bowl. Fold in the hot potato and onion and let the mixture rest 10 minutes so the potato absorbs the egg.
Return a little of the reserved oil to the skillet and pour in the mixture over medium-low heat.
Cook 6-8 minutes until the bottom is set. Flip using a plate and cook 4 more minutes.
Slide onto a plate and serve warm or at room temperature.

note: Removed spinach - a tortilla espanola is potato, egg, olive oil and salt, with onion as the one permitted variable; a third vegetable makes it a different dish. Potato 150 -> 300 g to reach the reference ~100 g per egg, which is the finding that actually changes the dish's identity (it was an omelette with potato in it). Oil 15 -> 20 g and the deep-pool confit technique moved into the step text, plus the missing reposo. Onion deliberately KEPT - the cebollista/sincebollista split is a genuine live dispute, not an error. Calories rise ~29%, which the report explicitly justifies; the solver's serving scale absorbs it.

steps: Rub the duck leg all over with the salt, black pepper, thyme and a crushed garlic clove. Cover and refrigerate 12-24 hours to cure.
Rinse the cure off the leg and dry it thoroughly. Melt enough duck fat to submerge it and poach at 90C / 195F for 2-3 hours, until the meat pulls easily from the bone.
Dice the carrot, onion and celery. Mince the remaining garlic.
Sweat the carrot, onion, celery and garlic in a spoonful of the duck fat until softened.
Add the green lentils, a bay leaf and about 200 ml of water or stock. Simmer 25-30 minutes until the lentils are tender but still holding their shape, then stir in the red wine vinegar.
Lift the leg out of the fat and crisp it skin-side down in a hot dry pan 3-4 minutes until the skin is golden and shatters.
Remove the bay leaf, spoon the lentils into a bowl and set the duck leg on top.

note: This was not confit: no salt cure, and a 130 g leg cannot be submerged in 'its own rendered fat'. Added the 12-24 hour cure, real Duck Fat to poach in, and the skin-crisping finish. Red Lentils -> Green Lentils: red lentils are specifically the ones that collapse to puree, and this dish is defined by lentils that hold their shape through a 30-minute simmer. Lentils 20 -> 60 g so they are the bed rather than a garnish, liquid rescaled from 2 cups (~24:1) to 200 ml, celery added to complete the mirepoix, red wine vinegar for the acid. Duck leg trimmed 130 -> 110 g to keep the much larger bowl inside the macro band.

originalName: Pan-Seared Duck Breast with Cherry Sauce & Brown Rice

recipe.name: Pan-Seared Duck Breast with Cherry Sauce & Potatoes

steps: Peel and slice the potato into thin rounds.
Score the duck breast skin in a crosshatch pattern. Season both sides with salt, black pepper and thyme.
Place the duck breast skin-side down in a cold pan over medium-low heat. Render the fat about 10 minutes until the skin is crispy and golden.
Flip the duck and cook 3 more minutes for medium-rare. Move it to a board and rest 5-10 minutes.
Pour off most of the duck fat, reserving it. Fry the potato slices in the reserved fat over medium heat 10-12 minutes, turning, until golden and tender. Season with salt.

Add the finely diced shallot to the pan and sweat 1 minute. Add the red wine vinegar and let it hiss away, then stir in the cherry sauce and the honey and simmer 2-3 minutes until syrupy. Take off the heat and swirl in the butter.
Trim the asparagus and steam 4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Slice the duck thinly across the grain. Plate with the potatoes and asparagus, and spoon the cherry sauce over the duck.

note: Brown Rice -> Potato: nothing about brown rice is French, and pommes sarladaises fried in the duck fat the recipe already renders and then throws away is the classic accompaniment. Renamed accordingly since the old name contained 'Brown Rice'. Removed the developer comment '(substituting for shallot)' that had leaked into a user-facing cooking step, and used real Shallot now that Phase A added it. Garlic dropped for shallot (the correct aromatic); sauce rebuilt as a real reduction - vinegar, honey, cherry, monte au beurre - instead of warmed jam. Roughly macro-neutral, -2.5% calories.
